title: ClickUp Brain2: The AI That Replaces All Your Software
lesson: A workspace assistant is presented through familiar work artifacts, concrete input/output examples and a contextual task, with a replacement claim framing the pitch.
opening: A ClickUp identity graphic becomes a crossed-out grid of other apps above the presenter. The visible contradiction supplies a reason to investigate the replacement claim. It is a promotional claim, not proven by the opening itself.
story_arc: Promise fewer tools → establish personal use → illustrate replacement → introduce AI capabilities → show generated work and an expanded deck → develop a context-aware lunch request into a response → close with a promotional offer.
payoff: The source shows several useful interfaces and artifacts, including a visible request-to-response chain. Most broad replacement and autonomous-work claims remain illustrative; the investor prompt and following deck are different examples.
selection_reason: Adds a long produced Short with many changes of information inside retained layouts, an extended prompt build, a real preview enlargement, and a multi-part contextual result. It is useful for deciding when a screenshot, diagram, presenter or full UI deserves the frame.
review_limits: Complete chronological 0.5-second source-frame sheets and machine-timed transcript inspected; listed native strips refine selected motions. No audio audition or uninterrupted realtime playback. Image-to-words reasoning is editorial interpretation, not known creator intent or retention evidence. Interval boundaries are approximate unless a native frame is cited.
